original_question: Let F be a free group of rank at least 2, and let H be a finitely generated subgroup of the direct product F x F. The membership problem for H in F x F asks for an algorithm that, given a word in the generators of F x F, decides whether that word represents an element of H. Does such an algorithm always exist for every finitely generated subgroup H of F x F?
target_in_paper: Conjecture 1 (Section 1, p. 3; developed in Section 3, p. 9): "There is no classical de Sitter solution with parallel sources." In the paper this is meant within the standard ansatz fixed in Sections 2.1-2.2 for smeared solutions on compact group manifolds with constant fluxes.
correct_elements: The draft has only the bare logical shape of a universal yes/no question. It asks whether a property holds for every object in a specified class. Beyond that, it does not match the paper's topic, notation, ambient theory, or target statement.
missing_details: The draft is on an unrelated group-theoretic decision problem; the paper is about classical de Sitter solutions in 10-dimensional type II supergravity with Op-planes and Dp-branes.
The paper's object is a classical de Sitter solution, not a finitely generated subgroup or a membership algorithm.

The ambient setup is 10d type II supergravity with only Op/Dp sources of a single size p, preserving 4d Lorentz invariance, with BPS sources and vanishing world-volume gauge-field pullback; none of this appears in the draft.

The paper restricts to the standard ansatz of Sections 2.1-2.2: a 4d de Sitter spacetime times a compact 6d internal manifold M, then further to the smeared case A=0, a compact 6d group manifold, and constant flux components in the flat basis.
The phrase "parallel sources" must be defined: sources wrap the same 10d directions, and in the paper this is the N=1 case, as opposed to intersecting sources with N>1.

The allowed flux components and structure constants are constrained by the orientifold projection; the relevant variables are the structure constants compatible with (2.9), the flux components allowed by (2.7)-(2.8), and the source terms T_10 (or T_10^I).

To be stand-alone and faithful to the paper, the question should say that the full remaining 10d Einstein equation, dilaton equation, flux equations of motion, and flux Bianchi identities must be solved; under the ansatz, the orientifold projection and Riemann Bianchi identity are automatic.

Section 3 narrows the unresolved part of Conjecture 1 to p=4,5,6 and records necessary conditions T_10>0, R_6<0, F_{k-2}≠0, and nonzero structure constants of the indicated types; the draft omits this narrowing.
The paper explicitly says the problem remains open even after these reductions, so the refined question should be posed as an open existence/non-existence problem, not as if the paper settles it.

There are no ambient ring/field, polynomial degree, or nilpotency conditions here; the missing stand-alone content is instead the supergravity ansatz, source geometry, flux data, and equations of motion.
refined_question: In the standard setup of Andriot's paper, namely 10-dimensional type II supergravity with only BPS Op-planes/Dp-branes of a single size p and vanishing world-volume gauge-field pullback, preserving 4d Lorentz invariance, and further restricted to the smeared ansatz A=0 with e^phi=g_s, a compact 6-dimensional group manifold M as internal space, constant flux components in the orthonormal basis subject to the orientifold projection, and all sources parallel (equivalently N=1), does there exist any classical de Sitter solution solving the remaining 10d Einstein equation, dilaton equation, flux equations of motion, and flux Bianchi identities? Equivalently, is Conjecture 1 true for this ansatz; and, since known constraints already eliminate the other cases, can one exclude such solutions in the only unresolved cases p=4,5,6?
justification: The draft does not target the paper's subject at all, so the closest recoverable official statement is the paper's first named open problem, Conjecture 1 in Section 1, page 3. Sections 2.1 and 2.2 make precise what counts as a "classical de Sitter solution" in this paper: type II supergravity with Op/Dp sources, the 10d metric and dilaton ansatz, then the smeared restriction A=0, compact group manifold internal space, constant fluxes, orientifold projection, and the finite set of remaining equations to solve (pp. 4-8). Section 3, page 9, shows that for parallel sources the unresolved part of the problem has already been reduced to p=4,5,6 and lists the necessary ingredients that any surviving candidate must have. Section 4, page 16, clarifies that "parallel" means the N=1 case. Section 6, page 29, confirms that the paper does not solve Conjecture 1, but identifies the remaining obstruction: one seems to need detailed internal Einstein equations, not just their traces. The rewritten question therefore stays as close as possible to the paper's actual intent, while making all hidden assumptions explicit and avoiding the unrelated subgroup-membership problem from the draft.
